 Home Education Today News Rajkot private schools defy Diwali break, pressure students to improve results Rajkot private schools defy Diwali break, pressure students to improve results
 Private schools in Rajkot allegedly called students for classes during Gujarat's 21-day Diwali vacation. Congress leaders questioned the Education Department's response after hundreds of students reportedly complained.
 advertisement Private schools in Rajkot allegedly called students for classes during Gujarat's 21-day Diwali vacation. (Photo: Screengrab/ITG video) India Today Education Desk Rajkot, UPDATED: Nov 18, 2026 18:15 IST Several private schools in Rajkot, Gujarat, have allegedly violated the state government's Diwali vacation schedule by asking students to attend classes during the declared holidays. Congress leaders have accused schools of putting academic performance and competition ahead of students' need for a break.
 According to the Gujarat government's academic calendar, schools must observe a 21-day Diwali vacation from November 5 to November 25. However, some private schools have reportedly continued academic activities during this period.
 advertisement Read More A HOLIDAY ON PAPER, CLASSES IN PRACTICE?
 Congress leader Rohit Rajput claimed that around 300 to 400 students had approached them with complaints that schools were forcing them to attend classes during the vacation.
 He also alleged that the matter had been raised with the District Education Officer (DEO) three to four times, but no concrete action had followed.
 Speaking to Aaj Tak, Rajput said students, including those in Class 11, had been called to Modi School and Kalyan School in Rajkot. Congress representatives visited the institutions and ensured that the students were sent home.
 He further alleged that school managements began sending students home as soon as Congress workers reached the premises.
 SCHOOLS ARE BEING ACCUSED OF PRESSURING STUDENTS
 Rajput claimed that private schools were continuing classes in the name of improving academic results and keeping students ahead in the competition. He argued that this placed an unnecessary study burden on children during a break announced by the government.
 advertisement The Congress representatives said vacations give students time to recover from academic pressure and spend time with their families. They maintained that schools should follow the government's holiday schedule instead of deciding independently to conduct classes.
 WHERE IS THE EDUCATION DEPARTMENT?
 The Congress leaders questioned the lack of action by the district education authorities despite repeated complaints. They said enforcing the declared vacation was the responsibility of the DEO, but the administration's alleged inaction had forced them to visit the schools themselves.
 They also demanded that the government ensure private schools follow the official holiday schedule.
 The incident has brought attention to the complaints against schools allegedly conducting classes during the Diwali break. Whether the Education Department will take action against the institutions remains to be seen.
 (With inputs from reporter Ronak Yogeshkumar Majithiya)
